la:prep:per.html:
per, prep. with acc. (by solecism with abl. PER QVO, =
whereby, Inscr. Miseni Repert. ex a. p. Chr. n. 159; ) [kindr. with Gr. παρά; Sanscr. pāra, ulterior; Lith. pèr; cf.: parumper, paulisper; v. ], denotes, like the Gr. διά, motion through a space, or extension over it.
Lit., of space, through, through the midst of, throughout, all over, all along: per amoena salicta raptare aliquem, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 40 Vahl.): inde Fert sese (equus) campi per caerula laetaque prata, id. ap. ( ib.): per amoenam urbem leni fluit agmine flumen, id. ap. ( ib.): per membranas oculorum cernere,: coronam auream per forum ferre,: iit hasta per tempus utrumque,: se per munitiones deicere,: per mare pauperiem fugiens, per saxa, per ignes,: per ignes,: per Averna,: per caelum,: per vias fabulari,in all the streets,: per totam urbem,: qui per provincias atque imperium tuum pecunias ei credidissent,in the provinces,: invitati hospitaliter per domos,: via secta per ambas (zonas),; : nascuntur copiosissime in Balearibus ac per Hispanias,in,: per illas gentes celebratur,throughout,: gustūs elementa per omnia quaerunt,.— Placed after the noun: viam per,: transtra per et remos et pictas abiete puppes,; .
Transf.
Of time, through, throughout, during, for: quod des bubus per hiemem,the winter through, during the winter,: nulla res per triennium, nisi ad nutum istius, judicata est,: nulla abs te per hos dies epistula ... venerat,during these days,: per decem dies ludi facti sunt,: per idem tempus,during, at, in the course of,; : per noctem cernuntur sidera,during the night, in the night-time,: per inducias,during,: per multa bella, : per ludos,: per comitia,: per somnum,: per tempus, during, i. e. at the right time, = in tempore, ; ; .—So distr.: per singulas noctes,; ; cf.: per haec,meanwhile,: per quae,.—
To indicate the agent, instrument, or means, through, by, by means of: statuerunt injurias per vos ulcisci,: detrimenta publicis rebus per homines eloquentissimos importata,: quid ais? vulgo occidebantur? Per quos? et a quibus?by whom? and by whose command?: quae domi gerenda sunt, ea per Caeciliam transiguntur,: quod nefarium stuprum non per illum factum est,.—Placed after its case: Exerce vocem, quam per vivis et colis,.—Esp.: per fidem decipere, fallere, etc. (= datā fide): per fidem deceptus sum, through confidence, i. e. in my host who betrayed me, ; ; .—So, per se, per te, through himself, by himself, of himself, etc.: homo per se cognitus, sine ullā commendatione majorum,: per me tibi obstiti, = solus,by myself,: satis per te tibi consulis,: per se solus,.—With ipse: nihil ipsos per se sine P. Sullā facere potuisse,: ipsum per se, suā vi, sua naturā, sua sponte laudabile,.—To form an adverb. expression, in, by, through, etc.: non dubitavi id a te per litteras petere,by letter,: per summum dedecus vitam amittere,in the most infamous manner, most infamously,: per iram facere aliquid,in anger,: per commodum, (cf. II. A. supra): per commodum rei publicae,; ; : per ludum et jocum,sporting and jesting, in sport and jest,; cf. , § 181: per vim,forcibly,: per dolum,: per otium,at leisure,: ceteris copiis per otium trajectis,: cibo per otium capto,: per tumultum = tumultuose,. —
To designate the reason, cause, inducement, etc., through, for, by, on account of, for the sake of: per metum mussari,: qui per virtutem perit, at non interit,: cum antea per aetatem nondum hujus auctoritatem loci attingere auderem,: per aetatem,: Druso propinquanti quasi per officium obviae fuere legiones,: ut nihil eum delectaret, quod aut per naturam fas esset aut per leges liceret,: cum per valetudinem posses, venire tamen noluisti,: per me, per te, etc., as far as concerns me, you, etc.: si per vos licet,: per me vel stertas licet,; cf.: sin hoc non licet per Cratippum,: fides publica per sese inviolata,: per me ista pedibus trahantur,: per me stetisse, quo minus hae fierent nuptiae,: si per suos esset licitum,: inspicere vitia nec per magistros nec per aetatem licebat,. —Hence, in oaths, entreaties, asseverations, etc., by a god, by men, or by inanimate or abstract things, by: IOVRANTO PER IOVEM, etc., Tab. Bant. lin. 15: per pol saepe peccas,; cf.: si per plures deos juret,: quid est enim, per deos, optabilius sapientiā?: per deos atque homines,: per dexteram te istam oro,; cf.: per tuam fidem Te obtestor,: nunc te per amicitiam et per amorem obsecro,: per pietatem!: per comitatem edepol, pater, etc.,.—In this signif. often separated from its object: per ego vobis deos atque homines dies, ut, etc.,: per ego te deos oro,; : per ego te, fili ... precor quaesoque, etc.,: per ego has lacrimas ... te Oro,; ; ; : per vos Tyrrhena faventum Stagna deum, per ego et Trebiam cineresque Sagunti Obtestor,; ; .—With ellips. of object: per, si qua est ... Intemerata fides, oro, i. e. per eam,; : per, si quid merui de te bene, perque manentem amorem, Ne, etc.,.—Sometimes to indicate an apparent or pretended cause or inducement, under the show or pretext of, under color of: qui per tutelam aut societatem aut rem mandatam aut fiduciae rationem fraudavit quempiam,: naves triremes per causam exercendorum remigum ad fauces portus prodire jussit,under pretext of,; v. causa: per speciem alienae fungendae vicis suas opes firmavit,: per simulationem officii,.—
In composition, it usually adds intensity to the signif., thoroughly, perfectly, completely, exceedingly, very much, very (very often in Cicero's epistolary style, and in new-formed words, as perbenevolus, percautus, percupidus, perbelle, perofficiose, pergaudeo; see these articles): pervelle, perfacilis, peramanter; sometimes it denotes the completion of an action, e. g. perorare, peragere; sometimes it is repeated: perdifficilis et perobscura quaestio,; so ; ; ; ; but also: perexiguā et minuta,: percautus et diligens,; cf. Madv. ad .—It frequently occurs in tmesi: nobis ista sunt pergrata perque jucunda,: per mihi mirum visum est,: per enim magni aestimo,: ibi te quam primum per videre velim, = videre pervelim,: Platoni per fuit familiaris,: per, inquit, magister optime, exoptatus mihi nunc venis,.—Per quam (also perquam), very, exceedingly, extremely: per quam breviter perstrinxi,: per quam modica civium merita,: per quam velim scire,very much indeed,: PARENTES PER QVAM INFELICISSIMI,.—As one word: illorum mores perquam meditate tenes,: propulit perquam indignis modis,: erat perquam onerosum,: perquam honorificum,.—Separated by an intervening word: per pol quam paucos reperias,.—Placed after the word it governs; v.supra, I. fin. and II. B.
